# ERC Recommendation 74-01, "Unwanted emissions in the spurious domain" (CEPT, approved 1998, corrected 23 May 2022)

**What this file is.** A transcription of the clauses this project CITES, not a copy of the recommendation. The
requirements registry's REQ-030 and REQ-071 (hardware EMCON, NEED-08) take their bench pass line from it under a
choice the session took on 27 September 2026 under the owner's standing rule of 26 September 2026: with EMCON asserted,
no emission above an analyser's displayed noise floor at any antenna port, measured in this recommendation's reference
bandwidths over its Table 1 range with the floor at least 10 dB under its Table 2 line for receivers and idle or standby
transmitters, and the VHF port, whose receiver owner ruling D-05 keeps listening, at or below that Table 2 line itself.
Filed 27 September 2026 (MESHSAT-1357, layer 3 closer). The kit claims no conformity with this recommendation (owner
ruling D-04: no CE, RED or EMC claim for the prototype); it is read here as a published measurement threshold.

## Introduction (page 2)

> This Recommendation specifies the limits of the unwanted emissions in the spurious domain (spurious domain emission
> limits) for different services and types of equipment. It should be used as a generic guide when drafting new and
> revising ETSI standards, and also for administrations in the absence of relevant standards. It should not be used as
> a stand-alone document for the purpose of placing products on the market under the Directive 2014/53/EU (Radio
> Equipment Directive) [1].

## Table 1, Frequency range for measurement of unwanted emissions (page 5)

| Fundamental frequency range | Lower frequency | Upper frequency (FUPPER) |
|---|---|---|
| 9 kHz - 100 MHz | 9 kHz | 1 GHz |
| 100 - 300 MHz | 9 kHz | 10th harmonic |
| 300 - 600 MHz | 30 MHz | 3 GHz |
| 600 MHz - 5.2 GHz | 30 MHz | 5th harmonic |
| 5.2 - 13 GHz | 30 MHz | 26 GHz |
| 13 - 150 GHz | 30 MHz | 2nd harmonic |
| 150 - 300 GHz | 30 MHz | 300 GHz |

> *The test should include the entire harmonic band and not be truncated at the precise upper frequency limit stated.

## recommends 4, the reference bandwidths (page 5)

> 4. that the following reference bandwidths should be used:

| Reference bandwidth | Frequency range (as printed) |
|---|---|
| 1 kHz | between 9 and 150 kHz |
| 10 kHz | between 150 kHz and 30 MHz |
| 100 kHz | between 30 MHz and 1 GHz |
| 1 MHz | above 1 GHz |

Its Note 5 (first two sentences): "As a general guideline, the resolution bandwidth of the measuring receiver should
be equal to the reference bandwidth as given in this recommend. To improve measurement accuracy, sensitivity and
efficiency, the resolution bandwidth can be different from the reference bandwidth."

## recommends 11 to 13 (page 7)

> 11. that, when measuring spurious emissions of receivers, no frequency range exclusion, such as the 250% of the
>     necessary bandwidth limit, quoted in recommends 1 should apply. Measurements should be made in accordance with
>     recommends 3, where the fundamental frequency range should include the highest oscillator frequency used in the
>     receiver and the harmonics are those of the highest oscillator frequency;
>
> 12. that the active state of a transmission station is defined as the state which produces the authorised emission;
>
> 13. that the idle/standby state of a transmission station is defined as the state where the transmitter is available
>     for traffic but is not in the active state.

## Table 2, Spurious domain emission limits, its last row (page 7)

| Type of service/equipment | | Limits |
|---|---|---|
| All other services, except those quoted above | Receivers and idle/standby transmitters | -57 dBm, for 9 kHz <= f <= 1 GHz; -47 dBm, for 1 GHz < f <= FUPPER (see recommends 11) |

The rows above it (fixed, land mobile and short range devices, space, broadcasting, radar and amateur services, each by
reference to an annex) are not transcribed; the annexes for land mobile and short range devices (Annex 2) and the
amateur service (Annex 6) carry receiver rows of their own that this project does not cite.

## How this project uses it

- The two levels are the published line between a station that is listening or idle and one producing its authorised
  emission (recommends 12 and 13); the kit's EMCON pass line keeps its noise-floor criterion and uses this line to set
  the analyser's floor and, for the listening VHF receiver only, as the limit itself.
- The reference bandwidths and Table 1's ranges are the measurement settings the pass line had left open
  (`v2/docs/feasibility/EMCON.md` section 6).
- Nothing here is a conformity claim, and a pass against this line is reported as a measurement of the prototype.
